title: Tenant priming and graceful-degradation runbook for hosted GPU exhaustion
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Follow-up ticket created from the 2026-03-02 GPU exhaustion incident impacting hosted API latency and tail errors. Deliver a focused runbook that combines rapid automated backfill (priming), per-tenant pacing, KV-cache guardrails, and a lightweight telemetry bridge so SRE and on-call can detect and recover from pool saturation in <10 minutes without manual tenant ejections.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-02 at ~14:04 UTC a sudden tenant traffic spike plus an admission scoring regression caused persistent queue buildup in several us-west GPU pools. Autoscaler hysteresis prevented timely capacity add and KV-cache pollution amplified per-request latency. Result: elevated 95/99 latency, several tenant tail timeouts, and a 24-minute partial degradation window before manual mitigations (soft-eviction of low-priority tenants and emergency pool priming) recovered service.
timeline: 2026-03-02 14:03 UTC - Spike begins from Tenant T-614; concurrent A/B test created elevated prefetching behavior
2026-03-02 14:06 UTC - Admission scoring regression increased prefetch factor for some tenants (automated scoring rolled in earlier that day)
2026-03-02 14:11 UTC - GPU pool queue depth exceeds soft watermark; autoscaler starts but hits hysteresis timer
2026-03-02 14:20 UTC - KV cache hit rate drops on hot models; long-tail token latencies climb
2026-03-02 14:28 UTC - On-call executes manual tenant soft-eviction and triggers warm-backfill playbook; traffic returns to baseline over next 24 minutes
2026-03-02 16:00 UTC - Post-incident triage begins; temporary mitigations validated
root_causes: Admission scoring regression (prefetch multiplier increased for a subset of tenants)
Autoscaler hysteresis + aggressive scale-down settings that delayed capacity add
KV cache pollution for the hot model shape increased serving latency and prevented quick queue drain
Insufficient cross-correlation telemetry between tenant admission/credits and GPU pool health metrics
mitigation_actions: Roll back admission scoring change (PR #3489) to remove the unintended prefetch multiplier - deployed 2026-03-03
Manual soft-eviction of low-priority tenants during incident to reduce queue pressure
Emergency pool priming (warm backfill) executed via ops script: redwood/tools/prime_pool.sh - used once for recovery
Short-term increase of autoscaler aggressiveness for critical pools (temporary config toggle)
KV cache TTL reduction for ephemeral keys on the hot model family to reduce pollution
long_term_actions: Implement automated priming backfill: controller will allocate N spare slots and prewarm with lightweight probes on sustained high queue slope (PR #3510)
Per-tenant pacing and budgeted admission: introduce per-tenant rate limiter tied to a credit bucket that decays under pool stress
KV-cache guardrails: eviction policy changes + adaptive TTLs for high-churn model shapes
Autoscaler fast-path: allow one emergency-add without hysteresis when queue growth rate exceeds threshold
Telemetry bridge: a small service that tags GPU-pool metrics with top contributing tenant IDs and admission signals for 30-day retention
Chaos/synthetic tests for tenant-whale scenarios added to nightly canary

decisions: Keep default prefetch multiplier capped at 1.25 until per-tenant pacing is in place
Automated priming will reserve up to 5% of GPU slots per-pool as warm-backfill (configurable per-pool)
Telemetry bridge will not include raw request payloads; only tenant IDs, model family, admission signals, and pool metrics to limit PII exposure
Require security review before increasing telemetry retention beyond 30 days
acceptance_criteria: Runbook available in Confluence with reproducible recovery steps and playbook links
Priming backfill implemented and validated in staging under synthetic whale load
Telemetry bridge dashboard surfaces top-5 contributing tenants within 3 minutes of a pool crossing the soft watermark
KV cache hit-rate recovers to pre-incident baseline in canary after adaptive TTL changes
No new admission-prefetch regressions merged without explicit codeowner approval
